title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

text.how-you-fall: You fall like mist settles: quietly, gradually, and then everything is soft and changed. Gye is the rain, the dew, the gentle water that soaks into everything. You don't fall for loud people. You fall for someone who feels like a secret, someone whose inner world seems as layered as yours. Often you fall in your imagination first, writing whole stories about a person before you've had a proper conversation. Your love is romantic, intuitive and deeply emotional. You sense what your partner feels before they say it. The danger is that your imagination can be more beautiful than reality, and you might stay loyal to a dream long after the actual person stopped showing up for it. Love the real one, too, not just the one in your head.
text.flirting: Your flirting is subtle, dreamy and a bit hard to catch. A shy smile, a song recommendation that says everything you won't, a meaningful look across the room. You're excellent at making people feel deeply understood, because you really do pick up on their moods. You often flirt through creativity: a drawing, a playlist, a poem in the notes app you might never send. The trouble is that many people miss your signals completely, and you'd rather vanish than risk being too obvious. Here's a gentle challenge. Send the thing. The playlist, the text, the "I've been thinking about you." Rain doesn't apologize for falling. And the people worth having are usually waiting for exactly that kind of quiet courage.
text.attachment: Your pattern can lean anxious, with a fearful streak. You crave closeness, but you also fear being truly seen and then left, so you might pull someone in and then go mysteriously quiet. Your moods shift like weather, and partners can find you hard to read even when you're simply feeling a lot. You sense every change in them, too, and can absorb their stress as if it were yours. When you feel safe, you're tender, devoted and astonishingly emotionally attuned, the kind of partner who knows exactly what you need on a bad day. The work for you is putting feelings into words and trusting someone with them. Your sensitivity isn't too much. It just needs the right person, and a little more saying instead of hinting.
text.jealousy: Your jealousy is quiet and imaginative. You don't need evidence. Your mind can build an entire storyline out of a like on a photo or a vague "I'll be out with friends." Your trigger is feeling emotionally replaced, that someone else might understand your person more deeply than you. You rarely confront it. Instead you retreat, become distant and dreamy, and wait for your partner to notice. If they don't, the story in your head gets darker. Here's the thing: your intuition is real, but your anxiety borrows its voice. Before acting, ask yourself which one is speaking. Then say the feeling simply. "I got a bit in my head tonight." Rain is gentle. Your honesty can be gentle, too.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you fall for fictional characters and real people who act like fictional characters. Emotionally unavailable, mysterious, "complicated," always just out of reach. The more unavailable, the more poetic it feels. Second flag: you hint instead of ask. You expect partners to read your moods like you read theirs, and when they can't, you feel unloved. That's a test nobody can pass. Third: escaping. When things get hard, you drift into your phone, your daydreams, your playlists, and leave the real conversation hanging. None of this makes you less lovable. It makes you a little lost in the fog. Pick someone who stays when the sky is clear, not just someone who makes the rain feel romantic.
text.what-you-need: You need emotional safety, more than anything. A partner who is gentle, patient and consistently kind, so your sensitive nature can finally relax instead of scanning for danger. You need someone who asks about your inner world and is genuinely interested in the answers, your dreams, your weird thoughts, the song that made you cry. You also need grounding. A practical, steady person can help you feel secure without dimming your imagination. And you need words, often. Reassurance said out loud does more for you than any grand gesture. The best person for you is like a calm lake for the rain to fall into. Quiet, deep, and always there when you land.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, you love like soft rain. Gentle, romantic, you feel everything they feel.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also wrote a whole love story about someone you've spoken to twice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just so intuitive! Your playlists are love letters.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Love letters you never send. Then you're sad they didn't reply.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Send the playlist. Quiet courage is your most beautiful kind.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: "Complicated" is not a personality. Stop dating mysteries. Date someone who texts back.

spring.intro: Spring is Wood's season, and Water nourishes Wood. A spring-born Gye Water is spring rain: gentle, intuitive and constantly feeding the growth around it. In love you are the person who quietly supports. You encourage dreams, listen deeply and seem to know what someone needs before they do. The season pulls your energy outward, so you can give until you feel invisible. You may hide your own wants because the other person's seem more important. Metal, your resource, is self-respect: your own values, your own routines, a partner who asks about your plans and remembers the answer. Rain is necessary for every garden. You are allowed to want to be the garden too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gye, you listened for three hours. They didn't ask one question. Notice that.

summer.intro: With Fire in command and Water controlling Fire, a summer-born Gye Water is a summer shower: brief, refreshing and gone before anyone can thank it. In love you are drawn to warm, magnetic people, and you are good at cooling their tempers and softening their intensity. But a light rain in July evaporates fast. You can disappear into a partner's bright personality, feel unseen, and leave quietly rather than ask for more. Your resource is Metal, which means clarity about what you need, and your own element is Water, which means friends, quiet evenings and reflection. You are not just their relief. You deserve to be someone's whole weather report.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gye, you're not their break from the heat. You're the person they should be thrilled by.

autumn.intro: Autumn hands command to Metal, the mother of Water. An autumn-born Gye is morning dew on cool stone: clear, perceptive and supported from beneath. In love your intuition is excellent. You sense a mood shift through a screen and can tell if someone is fibbing by how they type. With so much resource, your blind spot is living in your head. You build a whole relationship in imagination, testing scenarios and interpretations, while the real person waits to hear from you. Wood, your output element, turns intuition into action: saying the feeling, making the plan, being a little bold. Your read on people is usually right. Now let them read you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gye, the whole relationship already happened in your head. They haven't been told yet.

winter.intro: Winter is Water's own season, so a winter-born Gye is snow and mist: quiet, mysterious and deeper than it looks. You feel love intensely and show it subtly. Partners often fall for your enigma, then struggle to tell whether you are into them. You can retreat into fog when you feel exposed, and doubled Water makes you sensitive to the smallest change in tone. Fire, which is your wealth element, warms you into play and confidence, while Earth gives you steady ground to land on. In love that looks like a dependable, affectionate partner and the courage to state your interest plainly. Mystery is lovely. Being understood is lovelier.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gye, you're a beautiful mystery. Give them one clear clue tonight.

strength.strong: A strong Gye Water is steady rain that knows it is needed. With plenty of Water and Metal in your chart, you are intuitive, perceptive and quietly certain about people. In love you often know what your partner feels before they do, and you can use that knowledge to steer. Your blind spot is overpowering through insight: deciding what they really mean, testing them with silence, holding back until they guess correctly. Mystery becomes a game they keep losing. Say what you see and what you want. Your intuition is a gift. Shared openly, it becomes intimacy.
strength.weak: A weak Gye Water is a light mist that disappears in sunshine. With little Water or Metal support, you are deeply empathetic but easily absorbed by stronger personalities. In love you sense every mood shift, take responsibility for it, and shrink to keep the peace. Your blind spot is over-giving your attention while asking for almost nothing back. You might not even notice your own needs until you are exhausted. Name one feeling a day out loud. Keep your own friends close. A partner who loves you will want to hear your weather, not just enjoy your calm.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labelled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard, fast and loudly. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
